This Month

The theme of the month

The Reset

September is the return to routine. Not a detox, not making up for summer. Twenty-eight simple, high-protein meals with enough comfort for the shift into autumn and enough fresh colour that nothing feels heavy.

This month's focus

Protein first, always. Meals easy enough to repeat without thinking, built so that getting breakfast sorted and knowing your next meal is the whole strategy.

What to expect

Warm skillets, soups and creamy pasta alongside quick wraps, bowls and high-protein sweets. Comforting enough for September evenings, still light enough to feel good in.

How these meals support your goal

Every plate is high in protein and designed to be repeated. Pick your four favourites, keep them on rotation and the routine does the work for you.

Kassy's meal note

My biggest back-to-routine trick is making food easy before I am hungry. Get breakfast sorted, know what your next meal is and repeat the recipes you genuinely look forward to. Protein first, add colour, and keep it simple enough that you can actually stick to it.

03
🍒The Model Body ClubThe Reset
Challenge System

Monthly challenges

One shared challenge across your meals and your training, plus four weekly missions. This is the same challenge as your Training Plan, so you only run it once.

The Reset · 7-Day Challenge

One small habit a day for seven days. Tick them off as you go.

Day 1
Plan your four training slots and choose your meals for the next three days
Day 2
Protein at every main meal plus a 20-minute walk
Day 3
Track your weights and reps in your workout and hit 2 litres of water
Day 4
Complete one 10-minute ab workout and prep tomorrow's breakfast or snack
Day 5
Add fruit or veg to three meals and hit your step goal
Day 6
Complete 10 minutes of mobility or recovery and make one high-protein sweet
Day 7
Review your week: one win, one thing to improve, and book next week's sessions
Four weekly Reset Missions — one goal per week, each building on the last
Week 1 · Routine Reset

Choose your Gym, Home or Hybrid schedule, complete at least 3 sessions, log your starting weights and prep two grab-and-go food options.

Week 2 · Strength Reset

Complete the planned week and improve at least two tracked lifts by one rep, a small load increase or cleaner control.

Week 3 · Core + Consistency

Complete all four 10-minute ab blocks across the week, keep the rest day, and use the home version instead of skipping if plans change.

Week 4 · Finish Stronger

Beat Week 1 on one lower-body lift and one upper-body lift, choose your four favourite meal repeats and write down three habits to carry into October.

Optional: the 30-Day Reset Streak

Want a daily version? Score one Reset point for every day you tick all five: move as planned (workout, recovery session or a 30-minute intentional walk), protein at every main meal, 2 litres of water, your daily step target, and a 10-minute reset for tomorrow (prep food, stretch, plan your session or set up your morning).

🍒

Finish the seven days and tag @KassyAlicee so I can see your reset.

Your Plan

How to follow your meal plan

Same 28 recipes for everyone. Your goal sets your portions, your protein target and how much extra fuel you add.

Fat Loss Foundation
Lean, light + consistent
Base portions
Calories
Approx. 1,500–1,700 kcal per day.
Protein
Approx. 100–130g protein per day.
How to follow the meals
Use the recipes as written, keep portions moderate and repeat the meals that feel easiest.
If you need less food
Reduce carb or fat portions slightly before cutting protein.
Balanced Toning
Fuel training + stay lean
Standard plan
Calories
Approx. 1,700–1,900 kcal per day.
Protein
Approx. 110–140g protein per day.
How to follow the meals
Use one breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack each day, then adjust around hunger and activity.
If you need more fuel
Add a snack, extra fruit or a slightly bigger carb portion around training.
Glute Growth
Build shape + support recovery
Higher-fuel option
Calories
Approx. 1,900–2,200 kcal per day.
Protein
Approx. 120–160g protein per day.
How to follow the meals
Keep protein high and increase carbs around training so your glutes have enough fuel to grow.
If progress stalls
Check food, sleep and training consistency before adding more volume or cutting meals.
Simple rules
  • Prioritise protein at every meal.
  • Build meals around foods you enjoy.
  • Add vegetables freely.
  • Stay hydrated.
  • Repeat meals if it makes life easier.
Low-oil cooking

Use low-oil cooking methods where possible: air fryer, oven, grill, non-stick pan, water sautéing, lemon, spices and low-cal sauces.

Small changes like these keep meals light without losing any flavour.

🍒

Calories are a guide, not a personalised prescription. Protein, consistency and portion awareness are the priority.

Macros are estimates and may vary depending on brands, portion sizes and swaps. Use them as a guide.

🍒The Model Body ClubThe Reset
Make It Yours

Adapt & swap

Do not like an ingredient, or got something else in? Swap it. Keep the protein anchor, trade like for like, and the meal still works.

🍒
The golden rule

Keep the protein anchor, then swap like for like. If a swap lowers protein, add another protein source or increase the portion.

Animal protein

100g chicken → 100g lean turkey / 120g prawns / 120g white fish / 120g salmon. Adjust fats where needed.

Plant protein

180–200g tofu → 120–140g tempeh / seitan
or 150–200g edamame / lentils / chickpeas.

Eggs

2 eggs → egg whites / tofu scramble / extra protein powder depending on recipe.

Dairy-free

Milk → almond, oat or soya. Yoghurt → dairy-free high-protein yoghurt. Butter → dairy-free spread, olive, avocado or coconut oil.

Carbs

Rice, orzo, couscous, quinoa, gnocchi, pasta, potatoes, wraps, pitta, bread, oats and noodles. Swap like for like by portion.

Fats

Avocado, nuts, nut butter, seeds, olive oil and salmon. Keep portions moderate.

Veg & flavour

Swap veg one for one, fresh or frozen. Herbs, spices, lemon, lime, vinegar, mustard and low-cal sauces add flavour.

Sweet snacks

Fruit, protein yoghurt, protein bars, dark chocolate, rice cakes, dates, frozen grapes or homemade high-protein sweets.

🍒

Swaps are flexible. Keep the meal balanced, keep protein high, and choose what you actually enjoy.

Get Ready

Prepare once + pick your favourites

Make food easy before you are hungry. Do the prep once, then lean on the meals you actually look forward to.

Prep once
Prep your protein
  • Cook 2 to 3 proteins for the days ahead: chicken, turkey mince, salmon or prawns, or tofu.
  • Portion and store so meals come together fast.
Prep your base
  • Batch one or two carb bases: baby potatoes, jasmine rice, couscous or orzo, or gnocchi.
  • Wash and chop cucumber, tomatoes, peppers, lettuce and carrots.
Sauces + snacks
  • Mix one yogurt sauce and one punchier sauce: chimichurri, sweet chilli-lime or shawarma yogurt.
  • Keep one high-protein sweet ready to grab.

Strawberry Shortcake Protein Crumpets
A sweet, creamy crumpet breakfast that tastes like strawberry shortcake.

31g per serving
High ProteinDairy FreeVegetarian10 Min
Why you'll love it

Fast enough for a weekday but feels like a proper weekend-style breakfast.

Ingredients
  • 2 crumpets
  • 150g dairy-free high-protein yogurt
  • 15g vanilla protein powder
  • 100g strawberries, sliced
  • 10g maple syrup
  • 10g crushed oat biscuit or granola
Method
  1. Toast the crumpets.
  2. Mix the yogurt and protein powder until smooth.
  3. Spoon over the crumpets and add the strawberries.
  4. Drizzle with maple syrup and finish with a small amount of crumble.
Tips & notes

Swap strawberries for raspberries; use soy yogurt for the highest protein; toast the crumpets well so they stay crisp under the topping.

Why you'll love it

Fresh, bright and different from the usual pancake breakfast.

Ingredients
  • 40g oat flour
  • 1 egg
  • 100g egg whites
  • 15g vanilla protein powder
  • 100ml oat milk
  • Zest and juice of ½ lemon
  • 1 tsp poppy seeds
  • 80g raspberries
  • 60g dairy-free high-protein yogurt
  • 1 tsp maple syrup
Method
  1. Blend the flour, egg, egg whites, protein powder, milk, lemon and poppy seeds into a thin batter.
  2. Cook thin crepes in a non-stick pan.
  3. Fold and serve with the yogurt, raspberries, lemon zest and maple syrup.
Tips & notes

Keep the batter thin; use a very good non-stick pan; swap raspberries for blueberries or strawberries.

High ProteinDairy FreeMeal PrepNo Cook
Why you'll love it

Prep it the night before and breakfast is completely ready when you wake up.

Ingredients
  • 50g oats
  • 25g vanilla protein powder
  • 100g dairy-free yogurt
  • 100ml oat milk
  • ½ banana
  • 1 Medjool date
  • 5g chia seeds
  • Cinnamon
Method
  1. Mix the oats, protein powder, yogurt, milk and chia seeds.
  2. Refrigerate overnight.
  3. Mash the date with a little hot water to make a date caramel.
  4. Top the oats with banana, date caramel and cinnamon.
Tips & notes

Chill at least 4 hours, ideally overnight; loosen with a splash of milk before eating; use cinnamon or a pinch of sea salt to deepen the banoffee flavour.

Why you'll love it

A brunch-style breakfast that is satisfying without feeling heavy.

Ingredients
  • 2 eggs
  • 1 thick slice sourdough
  • 70g avocado
  • 100g cherry tomatoes
  • Handful of rocket
  • 1 tsp honey
  • Chilli flakes
  • Lime
  • Smoked paprika
Method
  1. Toast the sourdough and smash the avocado over it with lime.
  2. Poach the eggs and blister the tomatoes.
  3. Top the toast with the eggs and tomatoes.
  4. Mix the honey with chilli flakes, drizzle over, then finish with rocket and paprika.
Tips & notes

Use one egg plus extra egg whites if you want more protein and less fat; swap hot honey for chilli sauce; tomatoes can be served fresh or blistered.

Ingredients
  • 50g oats
  • 30g vanilla protein powder
  • ½ banana
  • 100g blueberries
  • 150ml water
  • ½ tsp baking powder
  • Cinnamon
Method
  1. Blend everything except the blueberries.
  2. Fold the berries through.
  3. Bake at 180°C for 20 to 25 minutes until just set and golden.
Tips & notes

Do not overbake; frozen blueberries work well; bake the night before and reheat for 30 to 60 seconds.

High ProteinDairy FreeKassy's Pick
Why you'll love it

A satisfying high-protein lunch that feels more substantial than another chicken bowl.

Ingredients
  • 120g lean steak
  • 200g baby potatoes
  • 50g mixed leaves
  • 80g cherry tomatoes
  • 50g cucumber
  • 15g chimichurri
  • Lemon
  • Black pepper
  • Quick chimichurri
  • Parsley, garlic, lemon, red-wine vinegar, chilli flakes, black pepper and a small splash of olive oil or water
Method
  1. Air-fry or roast the potatoes until crisp.
  2. Cook the steak to your preference and rest before slicing.
  3. Build the bowl with leaves, tomatoes and cucumber.
  4. Add the potatoes and steak, then spoon the chimichurri over the top.
Tips & notes

Rest the steak before slicing; air-fry the potatoes for the crispiest oil-light finish; keep the chimichurri parsley-heavy and thin it with lemon and water.

Meal-prep friendly, high in protein and packed with vegetables.

Ingredients
  • 150g lean turkey mince
  • 1 large red pepper, halved
  • 100g cooked couscous
  • 50g chopped tomatoes
  • Handful of spinach
  • 1 tsp harissa
  • ½ tsp cumin
  • 40g dairy-free yogurt
  • Lemon
  • Parsley
Method
  1. Roast the pepper halves for 10 minutes.
  2. Brown the turkey with harissa, cumin, tomatoes and spinach, then mix through the couscous.
  3. Fill the peppers and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes.
  4. Finish with lemon yogurt and parsley.
Tips & notes

Make two portions at once; swap couscous for quinoa; reduce the harissa and add paprika if you prefer milder heat.

Your Club

Keep going

September was never about undoing summer. It was about getting the routine back. Keep protein high, lean on the meals you actually like and let the rest flex. Here is how to carry it into October.

🍒
Pick your four repeats
That was Week 4's mission. Four meals you can make without thinking will beat twenty-eight you never cook twice.
🍒
Pair it with The Reset training
The training plan is the twin of this one: same theme, same seven-day challenge, same weekly missions. Pair the two, or let the meals stand alone.
🍒
Keep prepping ahead
The single habit that carried this month was making food easy before you were hungry. Keep that one and the rest follows.
🍒
Come back next month
A fresh drop lands every month: new meals, new theme, same simple approach.

If summer has been full of holidays, dinners and late nights, you do not need to make up for it. Start where you are, pick the meals you look forward to, and let the routine do the work.

Kassy
